chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Aban from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It is recommended to pray in the Mosque of Ghadir because the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) established the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) there, and it is the place where God, the Mighty and Majestic, manifested the Truth.

key_terms.أَقَامَ: Established/installed (in the context of authority or position)
key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْحَقَّ: The Truth (often referring to the Imamate or divine reality)
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الْغَدِيرِ: The Mosque of Ghadir, a specific location associated with the event of Ghadir Khumm
key_terms.يُسْتَحَبُّ: Recommended (a legal ruling less obligatory than wajib but more than mubah)

ai.seo_question: Why is it recommended to pray in the Mosque of Ghadir according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the spiritual merit of praying in the Mosque of Ghadir, linking it directly to the event of Ghadir Khumm where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) publicly designated Imam Ali (peace be upon him) as his successor. The narration highlights this site as the locus where Allah manifested the Truth (al-Haqq), reinforcing the theological significance of the location in Shia tradition as a place of divine confirmation and authority.
